note: AI-generated illustrations, made to follow the King James text; artistic interpretations, not historical records.

GEN-001.title: Light over the Deep
GEN-001.q: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light
GEN-001.alt: A vast primeval dark ocean beneath rolling clouds. Diffuse white-gold light emerges through the clouds and reflects across water.

GEN-002.title: Land, Seas, and Vegetation
GEN-002.q: let the dry land appear: and it was so
GEN-002.alt: A newly verdant coastline with rocky dry land, clear blue seas, grasses, seed-bearing plants and fruit trees under diffuse dawnlike illumination.
GEN-002.note: An artistic creation landscape; Genesis 1:9–13 does not identify each tree species or establish a dated cultivation scene.

GEN-021.title: The Lights of Heaven
GEN-021.q: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night
GEN-021.alt: A pristine coast beneath twilight, with the sun at the horizon, a crescent moon, and the first stars.

GEN-003.title: Life in Sea and Sky
GEN-003.q: Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life
GEN-003.alt: A pristine limestone coast with natural seabirds flying above clear shallow water and silvery fish visibly swimming beneath the surface. Spacious blue sky, soft cinematic sunlight.

GEN-007.title: The Garden of Eden
GEN-007.q: the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden
GEN-007.alt: A verdant garden with a clear river, fruit trees and abundant natural greenery. Quiet luminous cinematic landscape.
GEN-007.note: An imagined reach of Eden’s river, rather than a map of its four branches or a botanical identification of its trees.

GEN-008.title: Leaving Eden
GEN-008.q: the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden
GEN-008.alt: Adam and Eve, two adult Middle Eastern people fully clothed in modest rough animal-hide tunics, walk away from a lush garden into stony terrain. Solemn but hopeful.
GEN-008.note: Cherub anatomy, number two and arc are artistic interpretations; Genesis does not specify their detailed form.

GEN-029.title: Cain and Abel Bring Offerings
GEN-029.q: Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord
GEN-029.alt: Cain lowers his face beside a basket of grain while Abel stands behind a covered flock offering and a small portion of fat.
GEN-029.note: Interpretive visualization of Genesis 4. The passage does not describe the offering surfaces or a visible mechanism of divine acceptance; the covered animal portion is not fully visible.

GEN-004.title: Noah Builds the Ark
GEN-004.q: Make thee an ark of gopher wood
GEN-004.alt: Elderly Middle Eastern Noah, silver-gray hair and beard, sand linen and ochre cloak, inspects hand-hewn beams beside an immense elongated dark timber ark under construction. Three adult sons work with ancient hand tools.
GEN-004.note: Precise toolkit, alloy and ark dimensions are interpreted. Genesis 4:22 allows metal tools generally.

GEN-009.title: Animals Enter the Ark
GEN-009.q: There went in two and two unto Noah into the ark
GEN-009.alt: Pairs and small groups of realistic animals peacefully approach one broad side entrance of Noah’s immense elongated dark timber ark. Silver-bearded Noah in sand linen and ochre cloak oversees.
GEN-009.note: Representative pairs enter the ark as in Genesis 7:9 and 7:15. The image does not show the complete clean-animal inventory.

GEN-010.title: The Ark on the Waters
GEN-010.q: the ark went upon the face of the waters
GEN-010.alt: Exactly one monumental elongated roofed wooden ark floats on broad rain-dark waters with clearing light at the horizon. Entire ark visible surrounded only by water and sky.

GEN-011.title: The Returning Dove
GEN-011.q: lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off
GEN-011.alt: Silver-bearded Noah in sand linen and ochre cloak at an ark window greets a dove carrying exactly one freshly plucked narrow green olive leaf. Water and receding hills beyond.
GEN-011.note: Complete keel and actual Ararat topography are not certified.

GEN-005.title: The Rainbow Covenant
GEN-005.q: I do set my bow in the cloud
GEN-005.alt: Noah, same silver beard, sand linen and ochre cloak, and seven other adult family members look gratefully toward a natural rainbow over rain-wet ground. A massive elongated timber ark rests on higher ground with misty mountains behind.

GEN-012.title: The Tower of Babel
GEN-012.q: let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven
GEN-012.alt: An enormous unfinished stepped mud-brick tower in ancient Mesopotamia, adult workers in modest linen, fired bricks and bitumen, broad plain and coherent scale.

GEN-013.title: Abram Begins His Journey
GEN-013.q: So Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him
GEN-013.alt: Gray-haired Abram leads Sarai, adult Lot and a household woman with two loaded donkeys and a small regional flock across a rocky landscape.
GEN-013.note: Abram, Sarai and the adult Lot travel with a selected portion of their household. Genesis 12:4 states Abram was seventy-five; Sarai’s approximate sixty-five follows their ten-year age difference in Genesis 17:17. Their older appearance, pack donkeys and low settlement are illustrative, and this crop is not a household census. The rear-view sheep shows a woolly rump; a conspicuous fat tail is not visually established in this image.

GEN-006.title: Abram Beneath the Stars
GEN-006.q: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them
GEN-006.alt: Mature olive-brown Abram, dark curly beard beginning gray, sand linen and dark-brown wool mantle, stands outside a goat-hair tent beneath a realistic star-filled night sky. Subtle firelight and starlight, no personified God or fantasy stars.
GEN-006.note: Genesis 15 occurs after Abram is seventy-five and before he is eighty-six; ninety-nine belongs to a later scene. His exact apparent age is not measurable.

GEN-022.title: Sarah Holds Isaac
GEN-022.q: God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me
GEN-022.alt: Elderly Sarah smiles at the entrance of a pastoral tent while securely cradling infant Isaac in linen.
GEN-022.note: Sarah and Abraham are elderly. Their numerical ages come from Genesis 17:17 and 21:5 rather than measurement of the painted faces.

GEN-023.title: Hagar Finds Water
GEN-023.q: she saw a well of water
GEN-023.alt: Hagar gives Ishmael fresh water from a clay cup beside a wilderness well.

GEN-014.title: Abraham and Isaac on the Mountain Path
GEN-014.q: God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering
GEN-014.alt: Elderly silver-gray-bearded Abraham in sand linen and dark-brown mantle walks along a mountain path beside young adult Isaac, who carries firewood. Quiet reflective journey.
GEN-014.note: Fire container, knife material and Isaac age are interpreted; blade is concealed.

GEN-015.title: Rebekah at the Well
GEN-015.q: I will draw water for thy camels also
GEN-015.alt: Young adult Rebekah in modest sand linen and muted rust head covering pours water from a clay jar into a stone trough for camels. Abraham’s adult servant watches gratefully near an ancient village well at golden evening.

GEN-024.title: Isaac Welcomes Rebekah
GEN-024.q: she became his wife; and he loved her
GEN-024.alt: Isaac welcomes veiled Rebekah near a pastoral tent at evening as camels and attendants wait behind.
GEN-024.note: Isaac is forty in Genesis 25:20; exact apparent age cannot be measured. Veil coverage is interpreted; full caravan not shown.

GEN-016.title: Jacob’s Dream at Bethel
GEN-016.q: behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven
GEN-016.alt: Adult Jacob sleeps clothed with a stone pillow under his head in a rocky landscape. A luminous broad staircase links earth and heaven with a few modestly robed angel messengers ascending and descending.
GEN-016.note: Dream form and angel number are artistic choices; distant faces are unassessable.

GEN-025.title: Jacob Wrestles Through the Night
GEN-025.q: there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day
GEN-025.alt: Jacob wrestles with a distinct man at the rocky Jabbok ford before dawn; the opponent appearance is an artistic interpretation.
GEN-025.note: The opponent appearance and ancestry are unspecified. The scene does not establish Jacob subsequent gait.

GEN-017.title: Jacob and Esau Reunited
GEN-017.q: Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him
GEN-017.alt: Middle-aged brothers Jacob and Esau embrace on an open path. Jacob has dark curly hair beginning gray; robust Esau has a reddish-brown beard.
GEN-017.note: Cropped legs cannot establish a limp; the four hundred companions are outside this close composition.

GEN-018.title: Joseph’s Special Robe
GEN-018.q: he made him a coat of many colours
GEN-018.alt: Jacob presents Joseph with a colored robe as ten older brothers stand in two groups of five beside dark tents and a small flock.
GEN-018.note: Jacob gives Joseph his special robe in a selected gathering with Joseph’s ten older brothers. Younger Benjamin is outside this view; this is not a complete census of Jacob’s household.

GEN-026.title: Joseph Tells His Dream
GEN-026.q: Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren
GEN-026.alt: Young Joseph, wearing his colored robe, tells his dream to seated Jacob and ten older brothers beside dark tents.
GEN-026.note: Joseph narrates his dream to Jacob and a selected gathering of his ten older brothers. Younger Benjamin is outside this view; the dream’s eleven stars are narrated rather than pictured as a separate vision.

GEN-030.title: Joseph Is Sold to the Traders
GEN-030.q: sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver
GEN-030.alt: Joseph stands downcast beside the dry pit and his discarded colorful coat as men exchange a tied payment pouch before a camel caravan.
GEN-030.note: Selected moment of Joseph’s sale after he has been raised from the pit. The twenty silver pieces and caravan cargo are concealed; the landscape, dress and transaction arrangement are reconstructed.

GEN-027.title: Joseph Interprets the Prisoners' Dreams
GEN-027.q: Do not interpretations belong to God?
GEN-027.alt: Young adult Joseph interprets the dreams of the cupbearer and baker in a softly lit prison cell.

GEN-031.title: Joseph Interprets Pharaoh’s Dreams
GEN-031.q: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace
GEN-031.alt: Joseph addresses a seated Pharaoh wearing Egyptian royal headcloth and regalia on an ornate throne, with officials in linen nearby.
GEN-031.note: After shaving and changing his raiment, Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s dreams before receiving office (Genesis 41:14-36). Joseph retains plain linen without promotion insignia. The unidentified king’s royal headcloth, uraeus and lion throne draw on comparative Egyptian iconography; no dynasty or named Pharaoh is asserted.

GEN-019.title: Joseph Oversees Egypt’s Grain
GEN-019.q: Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much
GEN-019.alt: Shaven-headed Joseph in pleated Egyptian linen and a broad collar supervises workers storing and recording grain beside jars and masonry bins.
GEN-019.note: Joseph oversees grain storage after his appointment. Egyptian grooming and linen follow a comparative court setting; the granary and accounting area are a reconstruction, not an excavated Joseph building.

GEN-020.title: Joseph Welcomes His Brothers
GEN-020.q: I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt
GEN-020.alt: Mature clean-shaven Joseph in Egyptian linen and restrained gold collar embraces adult Benjamin in an ancient Egyptian chamber. Other adult brothers watch in astonishment and reconciliation.
GEN-020.note: Joseph wears an Egyptian-inspired linen court costume and collar. This close embrace of Benjamin shows only part of the brother group; the room is an illustrative reconstruction.

GEN-028.title: Jacob Blesses Ephraim and Manasseh
GEN-028.alt: Elderly Jacob crosses his hands to bless Ephraim and Manasseh as an older Joseph stands beside them.

EXO-001.title: Moses Among the Reeds
EXO-001.q: Because I drew him out of the water
EXO-001.alt: Pharaoh’s adult daughter securely cradles swaddled baby Moses beside an empty reed basket among calm Nile reeds, with attendants and Miriam nearby. The rescue is complete, and the child is safe.
EXO-001.note: Shows the infant held after the basket is opened. Royal sunshade and clothing details are comparative reconstructions.

EXO-002.title: The Burning Bush
EXO-002.q: the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed
EXO-002.alt: Elderly olive-brown Moses, silver-white beard, sand linen, muted indigo mantle and wooden staff, stands barefoot beside his sandals before a living desert bush burning yet unconsumed. Dawn, no person in the flames.

EXO-011.title: Moses and Aaron Before Pharaoh
EXO-011.q: Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh
EXO-011.alt: Moses and Aaron stand before Pharaoh while a serpent lies on the palace floor.

EXO-012.title: The Nile Turns Red
EXO-012.q: all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood
EXO-012.alt: Aaron extends his rod over the red Nile as Moses and Pharaoh watch from the bank.
EXO-012.note: An illustrative Nile settlement. Distant mudbrick fortifications are not a surveyed city or uniquely medieval architecture.

EXO-013.title: Frogs in Egypt
EXO-013.q: the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt
EXO-013.alt: Two Egyptian adults watch small frogs spreading through their mudbrick home.

EXO-003.title: The Passover Meal
EXO-003.q: with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand
EXO-003.alt: A modest Hebrew household at night eats roasted lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs, fully dressed for departure. Warm oil lamps, travel bundles and staff.

EXO-004.title: The Exodus Begins
EXO-004.q: all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt
EXO-004.alt: Elderly Moses leads families, loaded donkeys and livestock away from low Egyptian mudbrick buildings and a distant pylon gateway before sunrise.
EXO-004.note: Moses leads a selected early departure view with families, livestock and cloth-wrapped kneading troughs. Low Egyptian mudbrick buildings and a distant temple pylon provide a comparative setting; the exact town, route and hour are not established.

EXO-014.title: The Pillar of Fire
EXO-014.q: by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light
EXO-014.alt: A pillar of fire lights the distant route for a caravan traveling through the night wilderness.

EXO-005.title: A Path Through the Sea
EXO-005.q: the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left
EXO-005.alt: Moses leads families along dry ground between walls of sea water at night, with a luminous pillar behind the people.
EXO-005.note: Full crowd, sea-wall scale and miraculous pillar form are interpreted.

EXO-015.title: Miriam Leads the Song
EXO-015.q: Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand
EXO-015.alt: Miriam leads women singing and dancing with frame drums on the safe shore.

EXO-006.title: Manna in the Wilderness
EXO-006.q: This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat
EXO-006.alt: Families gather fine pale round grains of manna into baskets at dawn, with Moses and low woven shelters beyond.
EXO-006.note: Omer quantities and precise miraculous material cannot be certified.

EXO-007.title: Water from the Rock
EXO-007.q: thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it
EXO-007.alt: Established Moses stands beside a rock as fresh water flows into a small pool. Adults fill clay jars; grateful families stand at a distance in a rocky desert.
EXO-007.note: Shows water flowing after the strike in Exodus 17:5–6. The crowd, elders outside the crop and camp layout are reconstructed.

EXO-008.title: Mount Sinai
EXO-008.q: mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke
EXO-008.alt: An enormous rocky Mount Sinai wrapped in smoke and dense cloud with flashes of light above. Hebrew families gather safely at the foot outside a clear boundary.
EXO-008.note: Exact Sinai location, miraculous fire form and camp population are interpreted.

EXO-009.title: Moses Receives the Tablets
EXO-009.q: I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments
EXO-009.alt: Established Moses carries two simple stone tablets on a rocky summit within luminous cloud. Tablets angled away with no readable writing.
EXO-009.note: The tablet outlines are conventional; the KJV does not specify rounded or square tops. Fine inscription content is not certified at this angle.

EXO-016.title: Moses Intercedes for the People
EXO-016.q: Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people
EXO-016.alt: Moses kneels in prayer on rocky Sinai above a distant encampment.
EXO-016.note: Moses prays as in Exodus 32:7–14. The distant peaked tents and camp plan are illustrative.

EXO-017.title: Moses Breaks the Tablets
EXO-017.q: he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount
EXO-017.alt: Moses releases two stone tablets that crack on the ground as Joshua looks toward dancers around a small golden calf.
EXO-017.note: Selected instant of Exodus32:19. The tablet shapes and incised marks, calf form and camp are artistic reconstruction; the marks are not a transcription of the commandments.

EXO-010.title: The Tabernacle Completed
EXO-010.q: the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle
EXO-010.alt: A wilderness tabernacle within a rectangular white-linen court fence. Layered sanctuary tent with blue, purple and scarlet woven entrance, altar and basin, cloud rising above, respectful people outside.

LEV-005.title: Presenting the Burnt Offering
LEV-005.q: he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering
LEV-005.alt: An anonymous worshipper places his hand on a live bullock before a priest, outside a blue, purple and scarlet embroidered entrance screen.
LEV-005.note: An anonymous worshipper places his hand on the live bullock before slaughter, the presentation moment of Leviticus 1:3-4. Priest, courtyard, entrance embroidery and altar completion are reconstructed; the illustration does not certify exact court dimensions or the later stages of the sacrifice.

LEV-006.title: The Grain Offering
LEV-006.q: he shall take thereout his handful of the flour thereof
LEV-006.alt: A priest takes a handful of flour mixed with oil from an earthen bowl containing frankincense.
LEV-006.note: The priest takes the memorial portion before it is burned. The KJV term ’meat offering' here refers to this grain offering; vessel forms, ingredient appearance and court completion are reconstructed.

LEV-001.title: Aaron in the Linen Garments
LEV-001.q: shall be girded with a linen girdle
LEV-001.alt: Aaron ties his white linen girdle beside a bronze washing basin and court posts with metal-colored fittings in daylight.
LEV-001.note: After washing, Aaron ties the linen girdle over his plain linen coat, with the linen mitre, illustrating Leviticus 16:4. Bronze sockets and silver-colored court fittings follow Exodus 27 and 38; the post form, laver shape and surrounding arrangement are reconstructed, and the complete court dimensions are outside this view.

LEV-002.title: Lots for the Two Goats
LEV-002.q: Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats
LEV-002.alt: Aaron holds two plain lot pieces between two live goats held by attendants before the Tabernacle.
LEV-002.note: Selected moment before sacrifice and release. The material and handling of the lots, goat colors and Tabernacle completion are reconstructed.

LEV-003.title: Incense Within the Veil
LEV-003.q: he shall put the incense upon the fire before the Lord
LEV-003.alt: Aaron pours incense onto coals before a smoke-veiled mercy seat with two inward-facing gold winged guardians in a dark chamber.
LEV-003.note: Aaron places incense upon coals within the veil, with smoke rising before the mercy seat (Leviticus 16:11-13). Two gold cherubim face inward and downward over the cover (Exodus 25:17-22). Their human-headed winged-sphinx anatomy, the censer and the low-key chamber exposure are selected reconstructions.

LEV-004.title: The Scapegoat Released
LEV-004.q: he shall let go the goat in the wilderness
LEV-004.alt: An appointed man watches a live goat walk freely into uninhabited rocky wilderness.
LEV-004.note: The release is shown after Aaron’s confession and laying on of hands. Exact terrain, goat color and rope use are reconstructed.

LEV-009.title: Rejoicing in the Booths
LEV-009.q: ye shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days
LEV-009.alt: A family shares food in a leafy booth with palm branches in bright daylight.
LEV-009.note: An anonymous household rejoices in a leafy booth during the Feast of Tabernacles. Palm branches, boughs, food and the selected gathering illustrate Leviticus 23:39-43; booth construction and site are contextual reconstructions.

LEV-007.title: Aaron Tends the Lamps
LEV-007.q: to cause the lamps to burn continually
LEV-007.alt: Aaron pours oil into one of seven gold spouted lamps, whose small flames burn at projecting wick nozzles.
LEV-007.note: Aaron tends the seven oil lamps outside the veil, illustrating Leviticus 24:1-4. The flames issue from projecting wick nozzles, and the depicted pouring, lampstand decoration, garments and woven guardian motifs are selected reconstructions; hidden fittings and exact dimensions are not certified.

LEV-008.title: Twelve Cakes Before the LORD
LEV-008.q: thou shalt set them in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table
LEV-008.alt: Twelve round cakes sit in two rows of six on a gold table, with two small frankincense bowls and a priest nearby.
LEV-008.note: Flat rows follow the KJV’s ’two rows, six on a row'; cake shape, frankincense containers and table ornament are reconstructed. This perspective is not a measurement diagram. Woven cherub anatomy is an artistic regional comparison.

NUM-002.title: Fruit from the Promised Land
NUM-002.q: they bare it between two upon a staff
NUM-002.alt: Two adult Israelite scouts carry a pole with a large cluster of grapes, with figs and pomegranates visible in baskets, fertile Canaan hills behind. Believable natural harvest.

NUM-001.title: The Bronze Serpent
NUM-001.q: Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole
NUM-001.alt: Established elderly Moses in sand linen and indigo mantle stands near a high pole bearing one bronze serpent. Calm people look upward from a desert camp.
NUM-001.note: Shows people looking at the brass serpent after healing. Active bites need not be visible in the selected moment; serpent form and camp are reconstructed.

NUM-003.title: Balaam and the Donkey
NUM-003.q: he bowed down his head, and fell flat on his face
NUM-003.alt: Balaam bows beside his donkey as a messenger blocks the vineyard path.
NUM-003.note: Balaam face mostly hidden. Deep bow is selected after Numbers 22:31; forehead need not visibly touch earth. Supernatural appearance and weapon details are interpreted.

DEU-002.title: The Firstfruits Basket
DEU-002.q: I have brought the firstfruits of the land
DEU-002.alt: A farmer presents a firstfruits basket to a priest near an altar and colored linen entrance screen.
DEU-002.note: A firstfruits basket passes from an anonymous farmer to a priest before the altar, illustrating Deuteronomy 26:1-11. The chapter leaves the chosen place unnamed; this Tabernacle-type setting, family group, basket contents and entrance embroidery are contextual reconstructions.

DEU-001.title: Moses Looks from Mount Nebo
DEU-001.q: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes
DEU-001.alt: Established elderly Moses, alive and contemplative, stands on Mount Nebo overlooking the expansive Jordan valley toward fertile distant hills.
DEU-001.note: An imagined view from Nebo toward the land. Fertile valley, river width, greenery and distances are not a surveyed panorama.

JOS-004.title: Rahab Hides the Spies
JOS-004.q: hid them with the stalks of flax
JOS-004.alt: At dusk Rahab spreads flax stalks over two spies lying low on an earthen rooftop.
JOS-004.note: Selected moment as Rahab finishes concealing the two men under flax. The rooftop and town are reconstructed; this is not an identification of an excavated house. The scarlet cord belongs to a later moment.

JOS-001.title: Crossing the Jordan
JOS-001.q: the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood firm on dry ground
JOS-001.alt: White-linen priests stand firmly with the covenant ark on poles in the middle of an ordinary dry Jordan riverbed. Families cross farther behind.
JOS-001.note: Blue outer covering follows Numbers 4 as a reconstruction choice; Joshua 3 does not state its colour.

JOS-002.title: The Walls of Jericho
JOS-002.q: Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city
JOS-002.alt: Distant mud-brick Jericho walls give way in dust while an Israelite procession with priests and ram horns remains safely outside.
JOS-002.note: Covering colour follows Numbers 4 as a reconstruction choice. This does not establish a particular archaeological destruction date.

JOS-003.title: Joshua Sets Up the Covenant Stone
JOS-003.q: Behold, this stone shall be a witness unto us
JOS-003.alt: Elderly Joshua addresses the people beside a covenant stone beneath Shechem’s oak.

JDG-002.title: Deborah Beneath the Palm
JDG-002.q: she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah
JDG-002.alt: Dignified adult Deborah in modest warm linen and wool sits beneath a large date palm hearing attentive adults' petitions in the hills of Ephraim.
JDG-002.note: Deborah sits under a date palm. Distant buildings and vegetation are contextual details, rather than an exact Ephraim landscape.

JDG-003.title: Gideon and the Fleece
JDG-003.q: wringed the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water
JDG-003.alt: Gideon squeezes water from a fleece into a clay bowl on the dry threshing floor.

JDG-001.title: Gideon’s Lamps in the Night
JDG-001.q: The sword of the Lord, and of Gideon
JDG-001.alt: Gideon and a few adult men stand at night holding torches and ram-horn trumpets, with broken clay jars at their feet and distant camp lights.
JDG-001.note: Full three hundred and camp plan are outside view. The audit reversed the figure’s hands; original hand allocation was already correct.

JDG-004.title: Samson Carries the Gates
JDG-004.q: took the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts
JDG-004.alt: Samson carries Gaza’s wooden gates uphill beneath the midnight sky.

RUT-002.title: Ruth Stays with Naomi
RUT-002.q: whither thou goest, I will go
RUT-002.alt: Ruth walks hand-in-hand with elderly Naomi toward Bethlehem, carrying cloth bundles.
RUT-002.note: Ruth and Naomi on the road. The distant town, trees and landscape scale are illustrative.

RUT-001.title: Ruth in the Harvest Fields
RUT-001.q: she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers
RUT-001.alt: Adult Moabite Ruth in dusty linen and muted russet headscarf gleans fallen barley stalks from a sunlit field. Adult Boaz speaks respectfully from a little distance; harvesters stand behind.
RUT-001.note: Ruth gleans and speaks with Boaz. The distant town is an imagined setting, rather than a documented Bethlehem skyline.

RUT-003.title: Ruth and Boaz at Bethlehem
RUT-003.q: So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife
RUT-003.alt: Ruth and Boaz hold hands during a joyful Bethlehem blessing while Naomi stands beside Ruth.
RUT-003.note: A public marriage celebration after Ruth 4:9–13. The exact gate and celebration arrangement are reconstructed.

1SA-020.title: Hannah Prays at Shiloh
1SA-020.q: only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard
1SA-020.alt: Hannah prays with clasped hands while gray-haired Eli sits beside a sanctuary doorpost; distant lamps are unlit.
1SA-020.note: Hannah prays in sorrow while Eli watches by the sanctuary doorpost, the selected moment of 1 Samuel 1:9-13. The room and inward-facing woven guardians are reconstructed; the distant lamps are unlit in this chosen daylight view and the Ark remains hidden.

1SA-001.title: Samuel Hears the Call
1SA-001.alt: The boy Samuel wakes at night while elderly Eli sleeps in a separate room and seven small sanctuary lights burn near an inner curtain.
1SA-001.note: Samuel wakes to the call while Eli sleeps in his own place and the sanctuary lamp still burns. The room layout and human-faced winged-sphinx curtain motifs are selected historical reconstructions; the Ark remains behind the curtain.

1SA-002.title: David Is Anointed
1SA-002.q: Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren
1SA-002.alt: Elderly Samuel pours a little oil from a horn over the head of young shepherd David in Jesse’s modest household as adult brothers watch.
1SA-002.note: David exact youthful age is unspecified; full seven brothers are outside the crop.

1SA-008.title: David Tends the Flock
1SA-008.q: There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep
1SA-008.alt: Slender adolescent David watches brown-faced fat-tailed sheep and black goats on a Bethlehem hillside, holding a plain staff.
1SA-008.note: The youngest son David watches a small flock before Samuel summons him; the adolescent appearance and selected fat-tailed flock are historical interpretations.

1SA-004.title: David Plays for Saul
1SA-004.q: David took an harp, and played with his hand
1SA-004.alt: Young David plays a wooden lyre as King Saul listens in a quiet royal room.

1SA-009.title: David Brings Provisions to the Camp
1SA-009.q: David left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage
1SA-009.alt: Slender adolescent David turns to run after handing baggage to its keeper, with a loaded donkey, ten flat loaves and ten cheeses nearby.
1SA-009.note: David leaves the provisions with the baggage keeper and turns toward his brothers. A pack donkey is a comparative reconstruction; the KJV’s carriage denotes baggage here rather than requiring a wheeled vehicle.

1SA-003.title: David and Goliath
1SA-003.q: I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts
1SA-003.alt: David and the towering bronze-armored Goliath face one another in a sunlit rocky valley.

1SA-010.title: David Sets Aside Saul’s Armor
1SA-010.q: I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them
1SA-010.alt: David sets a bronze helmet beside armor while Saul watches in the camp.

1SA-005.title: David Chooses Five Stones
1SA-005.q: chose him five smooth stones out of the brook
1SA-005.alt: David chooses five smooth stones beside a brook, with sling and pouch ready.
1SA-005.note: Tiny fitting material and exact numerical age are unspecified.

1SA-006.title: David and Jonathan’s Covenant
1SA-006.q: Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David
1SA-006.alt: Jonathan offers his robe to David as a sign of their covenant friendship.
1SA-006.note: Sheathed blade material is unassessable. Jonathan can wear a plain inner tunic after giving his outer robe in 1 Samuel 18:4.

1SA-019.title: Music Welcomes David and Saul
1SA-019.q: the women came out of all cities of Israel, singing and dancing
1SA-019.alt: Women with drums and a small lyre welcome David and Saul with music at a town gate.

1SA-012.title: Jonathan’s Farewell in the Field
1SA-012.q: they kissed one another, and wept one with another
1SA-012.alt: David and Jonathan share a tearful farewell beside a field stone after the boy has departed.

1SA-013.title: David Receives Bread at Nob
1SA-013.q: So the priest gave him hallowed bread
1SA-013.alt: The priest Ahimelech gives David holy bread on a linen-lined tray at Nob.
1SA-013.note: Precise priestly outfit and loaf shape are not supplied by 1 Samuel 21; full sanctuary showbread inventory is not shown.

1SA-014.title: Refuge at Adullam
1SA-014.q: David therefore departed thence, and escaped to the cave Adullam
1SA-014.alt: David offers water to weary travelers at the safe entrance of Adullam’s cave.
1SA-014.note: Full four hundred refugees are outside view.

1SA-007.title: David Spares Saul
1SA-007.q: So David stayed his servants with these words
1SA-007.alt: David holds a cut robe corner and restrains his companions as Saul leaves the cave unharmed.
1SA-007.note: Matching the missing corner to Saul folded hem is not fully certifiable. David already held cloth in the original; no simultaneous 1 Samuel 24:8 bow is claimed.

1SA-015.title: Abigail Meets David
1SA-015.q: blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou
1SA-015.alt: Abigail speaks wisely to David beside donkeys carrying provisions, helping avert bloodshed.
1SA-015.note: Full gift totals are not shown. Container shape is interpreted; the KJV does not prescribe a complete bottle profile.

1SA-016.title: David Takes the Spear and Water Jug
1SA-016.q: David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster
1SA-016.alt: David and Abishai quietly leave Saul’s sleeping camp with his spear and water jug.
1SA-016.note: This selects the moment after the spear and water cruse were taken, rather than showing a duplicate spear still planted beside Saul.

1SA-017.title: David Finds Strength at Ziklag
1SA-017.q: David encouraged himself in the Lord his God
1SA-017.alt: David kneels in prayer amid the cooled, fire-damaged ruins of Ziklag.
1SA-017.note: The ephod’s form and Ziklag setting are reconstructed; no precise excavated layout is asserted.

1SA-018.title: The Recovered Families Return
1SA-018.alt: David and Abigail clasp hands as recovered families return safely with their belongings and flocks.
1SA-018.note: Full population and flock are outside view; woolly sheep are not categorically anachronistic.

2SA-005.title: David Mourns Saul and Jonathan
2SA-005.q: they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even
2SA-005.alt: David mourns with open hands after hearing of the deaths of Saul and Jonathan.
2SA-005.note: Exact age and full grieving company are unspecified in this close composition.

2SA-001.title: David Is Made King
2SA-001.q: they anointed David king over Israel
2SA-001.alt: Elders anoint the adult David as king in a sunlit Hebron courtyard.
2SA-001.note: The anointing by Israel’s elders in 2 Samuel 5 follows David’s reign in Hebron; the officiant is anonymous, not Samuel.

2SA-002.title: David Rejoices Before the Ark
2SA-002.q: David danced before the Lord with all his might
2SA-002.alt: David rejoices in a linen ephod as bearers carry the ark toward Jerusalem.
2SA-002.note: Ark covering follows Numbers 4 as a reconstruction choice. Linen ephod tailoring and city completion are interpreted; metal trumpets are also legitimate in the 1 Chronicles 15 parallel.

2SA-004.title: David’s Prayer of Gratitude
2SA-004.q: Who am I, O Lord God? and what is my house
2SA-004.alt: David prays gratefully with open hands at the entrance to the ark’s tent.
2SA-004.note: Open tent access is a compositional reconstruction. Human-headed winged sphinx anatomy is the selected ancient Near Eastern interpretation, not a KJV specification.

2SA-006.title: A Place at David’s Table
2SA-006.q: thou shalt eat bread at my table continually
2SA-006.alt: David welcomes Mephibosheth to his table, with foot support and a walking aid beside the chair.
2SA-006.note: The support and wraps are inferred; the picture retains Mephibosheth’s disability without asserting a modern diagnosis.

2SA-003.title: Nathan Speaks to David
2SA-003.q: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man.
2SA-003.alt: Nathan speaks earnestly to King David, who listens with a chastened expression.

2SA-007.title: David on the Mount of Olives
2SA-007.q: David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up
2SA-007.alt: David climbs the Mount of Olives barefoot in grief, with his face visible beneath a linen head covering.

2SA-008.title: David Buys the Threshing Floor
2SA-008.q: So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
2SA-008.alt: Older David pours irregular silver fragments from a cloth pouch into Araunah’s hands beside a table, with yoked oxen and a threshing sledge behind.
2SA-008.note: David pays Araunah for the threshing floor and oxen, refusing to offer to the LORD what costs him nothing. The selected source is 2 Samuel 24:24, which names fifty shekels of silver; the visible hacksilver is illustrative and does not certify that weight.

1KI-005.title: David Gives Solomon His Charge
1KI-005.q: be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man
1KI-005.alt: Elderly David gives counsel to the attentive young Solomon in a quiet royal chamber.
1KI-005.note: David’s approximate age follows the narrative chronology; the degree of frailty and room arrangement are interpreted.

1KI-006.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
1KI-006.q: In Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night
1KI-006.alt: Solomon sleeps at Gibeon during a luminous dream of asking for wisdom.
1KI-006.note: Selected Gibeon dream setting. The room and unpersonified light are artistic completion; the striped wall cloth is a generic textile, not a worn ritual shawl.

1KI-001.title: The Temple of Solomon
1KI-001.q: the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord.
1KI-001.alt: Linen-clothed priests emerge through a cloud-filled Temple entrance between bronze pillars and doors carved with human-faced winged motifs, palms and flowers.
1KI-001.note: Priests emerge as the cloud fills Solomon’s Temple at its dedication. The doors show carved cherubim, palms and flowers; their human-faced winged-sphinx anatomy is a selected historical reconstruction. The Ark and inner oracle figures remain unseen.

1KI-008.title: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
1KI-008.q: behold, the half was not told me
1KI-008.alt: Solomon and the Queen of Sheba converse in a portico while attendants bring gifts.
1KI-008.note: The Queen’s precise homeland, ancestry, dress and palace setting are not supplied by the KJV; this is a selected regional visualization.

1KI-002.title: Elijah and the Ravens
1KI-002.q: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning
1KI-002.alt: Elijah sits beside a brook as one raven brings bread and another stands beside a small portion of meat on a rock.
1KI-002.note: Portion quantities and cooking state are artistic choices.

1KI-007.title: Elijah and the Widow’s Flour
1KI-007.q: The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail
1KI-007.alt: The widow pours flour into a bowl as Elijah speaks reassuringly in her courtyard.

1KI-003.title: Fire on Mount Carmel
1KI-003.q: Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice
1KI-003.alt: Elijah raises his hands beside an offering on a low stone altar as fire descends from above; a water-filled trench and four jars surround it, and the people lie prostrate behind.

1KI-004.title: Elijah at the Cave
1KI-004.q: he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave.
1KI-004.alt: Same Elijah stands at a cave mouth in gentle dawn light, his mantle covering his mouth and nose while leaving eyes visible. Vast quiet mountain panorama, no personified God.
1KI-004.note: Elijah at an imagined Horeb cave. Sparse shrubs do not contradict the arid setting; exact site and vegetation are uncertain.

2KI-005.title: Elijah’s Mantle Falls to Elisha
2KI-005.q: He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him
2KI-005.alt: Bald-crowned Elisha watches as Elijah ascends in a whirlwind above a falling mantle, separated from a fiery chariot and horses.
2KI-005.note: Elisha cries out as Elijah ascends in the whirlwind, separate from the fiery chariot. The falling mantle is an inferred visual transition before its recovery; the text does not specify its trajectory.

2KI-009.title: The Widow’s Oil Fills the Vessels
2KI-009.q: shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.
2KI-009.alt: Behind a shut door, a widow pours oil into borrowed clay jars while her two sons bring and hold vessels.
2KI-009.note: The pouring takes place behind a shut door with the widow and her two sons, as in verses4–5. Elisha is not shown inside. Household, vessel forms and the sons' ages are reconstructed.

2KI-004.title: The Shunammite’s Son Restored
2KI-004.alt: A mother embraces her restored son as bald-crowned Elisha stands nearby in a plain upper room with a bed, low stand and backless stool.
2KI-004.note: After bowing in thanks, the Shunammite embraces her restored son with Elisha nearby. The simple bed, low stand, stool and unlit oil lamp are a comparative reconstruction of the chamber furnishings.

2KI-001.title: Naaman at the Jordan
2KI-001.q: his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
2KI-001.alt: Naaman stands safely in the shallow Jordan in modest wet linen, healthy after washing, attendants on shore.

2KI-010.title: The Iron Axe Head Floats
2KI-010.q: And he cut down a stick, and cast it in thither; and the iron did swim.
2KI-010.alt: Balding Elisha gestures as a man reaches for a detached axe head floating beside a cut stick in the Jordan.
2KI-010.note: The floating iron and retrieval follow verses6–7. Tool forms, riverbank and dwelling framework are reconstructed; the illustration does not establish the exact axe design or location.

2KI-002.title: Hezekiah’s Prayer
2KI-002.q: Hezekiah went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.
2KI-002.alt: Hezekiah prays in sackcloth before a spread letter in a stone Temple court; an unlit clay lamp and low flat-roofed houses are nearby.
2KI-002.note: Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter before the LORD and prays. His sackcloth follows the earlier scene in 2 Kings 19:1; the low Iron Age settlement and Temple court are comparative reconstructions, and the daylight lamp is unlit.

2KI-003.title: The Book of the Law Is Found
2KI-003.q: I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord.
2KI-003.alt: Hilkiah and Shaphan respectfully hold the discovered scroll in a stone and timber Temple room, writing hidden.
2KI-003.note: The written side and some priestly clothing are hidden. The ancillary room is reconstructed, not a recovered plan.

2KI-006.title: Josiah Reads the Covenant
2KI-006.q: the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord
2KI-006.alt: King Josiah reads a scroll beside a bronze pillar as a varied assembly listens in the First Temple court.
2KI-006.note: A selected close view of Josiah reading beside a pillar. The crowd represents the larger assembly; the king’s appearance and court completion are reconstructed.

2KI-007.title: Jerusalem Burns and Its Walls Fall
2KI-007.q: brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
2KI-007.alt: Babylonian troops dismantle Jerusalem’s stone wall with ropes and levers as houses and the Temple’s timber roof burn behind them.
2KI-007.note: Reconstructed selected view of the burning and wall demolition. Excavated late Iron Age destruction informs stone, plaster and charred timber; the complete street, soldiers and Temple completion are interpretive.

2KI-008.title: Carried Away from Jerusalem
2KI-008.q: But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.
2KI-008.alt: Families leave ruined Jerusalem under Babylonian guard while poor workers remain among vines and fields at left.
2KI-008.note: Representative deportees and the poor left to cultivate the land are shown together. Individuals, route, buildings and their relative positions are reconstructed; population totals are not depicted.

EZR-002.title: Cyrus Proclaims the Return
EZR-002.q: he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing
EZR-002.alt: Cyrus sits holding a scroll as a herald reads his proclamation to gathered Judean elders and Persian officials.
EZR-002.note: Reconstructed proclamation scene following Ezra 1. Cyrus’s appearance and court are artistic; the Cyrus Cylinder supplies wider historical context, not the text of Ezra’s decree.

EZR-003.title: The Temple Vessels Are Returned
EZR-003.q: Cyrus the king brought forth the vessels of the house of the Lord
EZR-003.alt: Mithredath hands a gold bowl to Sheshbazzar beside representative gold and silver vessels, baskets and simple knives.
EZR-003.note: A selected handover of representative vessels, not a picture of the complete 5,400-object inventory. The vessels' forms, room and personal appearances are reconstructed.

EZR-001.title: The Temple Foundation Is Laid
EZR-001.q: could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people
EZR-001.alt: Priests and Levites celebrate the temple foundation while older witnesses weep among the rejoicing crowd.
EZR-001.note: Silver trumpets are retained after Ezra 3 and Numbers 10; ram horns are not a universal replacement for biblical metal trumpets.

NEH-001.title: Jerusalem’s Wall Rebuilt
NEH-001.q: So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty and two days.
NEH-001.alt: Nehemiah and workers stand beside the completed wall and an open unfinished gateway of Persian-period Jerusalem.
NEH-001.note: Selected moment with wall complete and gateway doors still pending, informed by Nehemiah 6:1 and 7:1; this does not certify an excavated wall course.

NEH-002.title: Ezra Reads the Law
NEH-002.q: Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood
NEH-002.alt: Ezra reads a scroll from a raised wooden platform while men,women and children stand listening below.
NEH-002.note: A cropped reading scene showing only part of Ezra’s platform and assembly. All thirteen named companions are not depicted. Personal appearances, scroll support and Water Gate completion are reconstructed.

EST-001.title: Esther Before the King
EST-001.q: the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand.
EST-001.alt: Esther approaches with dignity as King Ahasuerus extends his golden scepter within a Persian royal court.
EST-001.note: Esther approaches the offered sceptre before touching it. Persian-inspired patterned garments, caps and palace details are comparative reconstructions, not exact Susa artifacts.

EST-002.title: Esther’s Banquet
EST-002.q: The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman.
EST-002.alt: Esther speaks to Ahasuerus at a private banquet as Haman watches uneasily.
EST-002.note: The banquet uses couches and a low table. The speakers can rise from a reclined position; precise caps, fabrics and room details are reconstructed.

JOB-001.title: Job in Humble Reflection
JOB-001.q: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
JOB-001.alt: Job in a worn plain robe sits on dusty ground beneath an immense sky, reflecting humbly without graphic sores.
JOB-001.note: Exact Job site, date and portrait age are not specified.

PSA-001.title: The Shepherd’s Green Pastures
PSA-001.q: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
PSA-001.alt: An anonymous shepherd sits beside quiet water with a straight staff and a short club rod, comforting a brown-faced sheep near fat-tailed sheep and two black goats.
PSA-001.note: An anonymous shepherd with a rod and plain staff rests beside quiet water, a poetic visualization of Psalm 23. Regional fat-tailed sheep and black goats supply comparative pastoral detail; the figure is not identified as David or as a literal appearance of the LORD.

PSA-002.title: By the Rivers of Babylon
PSA-002.q: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
PSA-002.alt: Grieving Judean exiles sit by a Babylonian waterway beneath hanging lyres as captors demand a song.
PSA-002.note: Poetic illustration of Psalms 137:1-4. The anonymous gathering, river, lyre forms and willow appearance are reconstructed.

PRO-001.title: Wisdom More Precious than Treasure
PRO-001.q: She is more precious than rubies
PRO-001.alt: Symbolic scrolls, an olive branch and a clay oil lamp rest beside irregular silver fragments, a plain gold ring and rough-polished colored stones.
PRO-001.note: An undated symbolic assemblage of wisdom and value; exact minerals and metal weights are not certified.

ECC-001.title: A Time for Every Season
ECC-001.q: a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted
ECC-001.alt: One continuous ancient autumn landscape with adults planting, tending and harvesting in adjacent field areas.
ECC-001.note: A symbolic visualization of seasons in Ecclesiastes 3. Tree species, crop calendar and simple cart are artistic choices.

ISA-002.title: Isaiah in the Temple
ISA-002.q: I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
ISA-002.alt: Isaiah kneels beneath two six-winged seraphim before a high throne concealed by glory, with a woven robe train spread across the steps and floor.
ISA-002.note: Visionary forms, exact wing folding and Temple setting are artistic interpretation, rather than a surveyed room or visible historical portrait.

ISA-001.title: On Eagles' Wings
ISA-001.q: they shall mount up with wings as eagles
ISA-001.alt: A natural golden eagle soars above vast Judean mountain ranges beneath a luminous break in the clouds.

JER-001.title: At the Potter’s House
JER-001.q: as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are ye in mine hand
JER-001.alt: Jeremiah quietly watches a potter reshape clay on a simple ancient wheel in a humble sunlit workshop.
JER-001.note: Specific wheel, site and town plan are interpreted. Selected instant between marring and remaking follows Jeremiah 18:4.

JER-002.title: Baruch Writes Jeremiah’s Words
JER-002.q: Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord
JER-002.alt: Jeremiah dictates while Baruch writes with reed pen and ink on a roll; low flat-roofed dwellings appear outside.
JER-002.note: Jeremiah dictates the words of the LORD, and Baruch writes them with ink upon a roll (Jeremiah 36:4,18). The room, working furniture and small view of low Iron Age dwellings are reconstructed; the skyline does not identify a recovered street.

JER-003.title: Jehoiakim Burns the Scroll
JER-003.q: he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth
JER-003.alt: Jehoiakim cuts and burns a plain rolled scroll over a brazier while Jehudi reads and three officials plead nearby.
JER-003.note: In the winter house, Jehoiakim cuts and burns the roll as Jehudi reads, while Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah plead with him (Jeremiah 36:21-26). The scroll has plain rolled sheet edges; the room, snow and small Iron Age town view are reconstructed. Jeremiah and Baruch are hidden elsewhere.

EZK-001.title: Life Restored in the Valley
EZK-001.q: the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.
EZK-001.alt: Ezekiel overlooks a broad valley filled with living adults in modest linen, restored hope in morning light.
EZK-001.note: Symbolic restoration of Israel after Ezekiel 37:10–14. This living mixed host represents the restored people, rather than the earlier dry-bone stage or a measured military formation.

DAN-004.title: Daniel Requests Pulse and Water
DAN-004.q: let them give us pulse to eat, and water to drink.
DAN-004.alt: Young Daniel in court linen presents pulse and a cup of water to an overseer in a fringed Neo-Babylonian robe.
DAN-004.note: Daniel asks Melzar for a ten-day trial of pulse to eat and water to drink instead of the royal portion (Daniel 1:8-16). His clean trainee’s linen and Melzar’s finished fringed court garments distinguish their roles; precise costume, vessel decoration and Babylon viewpoint are period-informed reconstructions.

DAN-002.title: Four Figures in the Furnace
DAN-002.q: Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt
DAN-002.alt: Three clothed men and a dark-haired fourth figure in radiant white stand unharmed and unbound in a fiery brick furnace.
DAN-002.note: Three men are unharmed and unbound with a fourth figure in the furnace (Daniel3:24-27). Nebuchadnezzar observes in the account but is offscreen in this image. The fourth figure’s dark-haired Near Eastern appearance and radiance are artistic choices, not a textual claim about his ethnicity or exact face.

DAN-003.title: Daniel Prays at the Window
DAN-003.q: he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God
DAN-003.alt: Daniel prays beside an open upper-room window while two officials watch from the doorway.
DAN-003.note: Daniel prays at an open window. Officials' patterned robes, soft caps and the Babylon panorama are illustrative; compass direction and the actual Jerusalem bearing are not visually certified.

DAN-001.title: Daniel Among the Lions
DAN-001.q: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths
DAN-001.alt: Daniel stands calmly within a stone den while several natural lions rest peacefully at a safe distance.
DAN-001.note: An interior view at the morning rescue in Daniel 6:19–23. The earlier sealed condition has ended; the king is outside this composition.

JON-002.title: Jonah Asleep During the Storm
JON-002.q: Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
JON-002.alt: A concerned captain wakes Jonah in the ship’s lower hold as a storm rages above.
JON-002.note: Jonah eyes are closed; exact ship fittings are reconstructed. This does not assert every ancient barrel impossible.

JON-001.title: Jonah Returns to Dry Land
JON-001.q: it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
JON-001.alt: Jonah sits safely on dry shore in a wet robe while the great fish’s back remains far out at sea.

JON-003.title: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
JON-003.q: Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
JON-003.alt: Jonah preaches to attentive people wearing sackcloth in a street of Nineveh.
JON-003.note: Repentant people at an imagined Nineveh gate. Assyrian-inspired motifs and sackcloth are reconstructed; the exact gate and ancestry of figures are not certified.

MAT-015.title: Joseph’s Dream
MAT-015.q: the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream
MAT-015.alt: Sleeping Joseph receives a radiant dark-haired messenger in a dream inside a modest night-lit home.
MAT-015.note: Joseph of Nazareth receives the angel’s message in a dream (Matthew 1:20–24). The radiant messenger’s olive-brown complexion and dark hair follow the project’s artistic design, not a textual claim about angelic ancestry; the home is contextual reconstruction.

MAT-001.title: The Magi Visit
MAT-001.q: they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
MAT-001.alt: Eastern adult travelers present gold, incense and myrrh to a fully clothed young Jesus seated safely on Mary’s lap in a humble house.
MAT-001.note: The visitors' count, ancestry and exact clothing are artistic choices. Matthew describes a house and child without specifying the child’s exact elapsed age; background is not a surveyed Bethlehem view.

MAT-002.title: The Journey to Egypt
MAT-002.q: he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt
MAT-002.alt: Mary safely cradles warmly wrapped young Jesus on a calm donkey while Joseph walks beside her on a broad level desert path toward dawn.

MAT-003.title: John Beside the Jordan
MAT-003.q: Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
MAT-003.alt: John the Baptist, weathered olive-brown face, coarse dark beard and unkempt dark hair, rough camel-hair garment and leather belt, preaches peacefully to attentive adults beside the Jordan.

MAT-004.title: The Baptism of Jesus
MAT-004.q: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
MAT-004.alt: Jesus, early-thirties Galilean Jewish man, olive-brown skin, dark eyes, shoulder-length dark wavy hair and short full beard, opaque off-white linen and earth-brown mantle, stands beside John during baptism in the shallow Jordan. Natural dove descends; no human God.

MAT-005.title: Jesus in the Wilderness
MAT-005.q: Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness
MAT-005.alt: Jesus with established identity sits alone on a rock in quiet prayer within a vast austere Judean wilderness. Dusty off-white linen and brown mantle, natural dawn light, no halo or cartoon devil.

MAT-006.title: The Sermon on the Mount
MAT-006.q: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
MAT-006.alt: Jesus teaches from a grassy hillside to attentive local families, with the Sea of Galilee beyond.

MAT-007.title: Teaching the Lord’s Prayer
MAT-007.q: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
MAT-007.alt: An intimate view of Jesus teaching prayer to three listening adult disciples on a Galilean hillside.
MAT-007.note: Distant roofs and vegetation are contextual details; a cypress-like tree alone does not date this scene.

MAT-023.title: The Wise Builder Builds on Rock
MAT-023.q: a wise man, which built his house upon a rock
MAT-023.alt: An anonymous builder checks a stone wall with a plumb line above a continuous exposed bedrock foundation.
MAT-023.note: Illustration of Jesus’s parable, showing the construction stage. The house and tools are contextual reconstruction; this is not an identified historical building.

MAT-024.title: The House on Sand Falls
MAT-024.q: and it fell: and great was the fall of it.
MAT-024.alt: Floodwater washes sand from beneath a collapsing house during wind and rain while another house stands on higher bedrock.
MAT-024.note: Illustration of the parable. The falling house follows verses26–27; the standing house on rock provides context from verses24–25. House forms, people and storm appearance are artistic reconstruction.

MAT-017.title: The Centurion’s Request
MAT-017.q: speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
MAT-017.alt: Jesus listens to a respectful unhelmeted centurion asking for help for his servant.
MAT-017.note: The centurion’s simple clothing is a conservative reconstruction; Matthew 8 does not specify his regiment or ancestry.

MAT-018.title: Peter’s Mother-in-Law Is Restored
MAT-018.q: he touched her hand, and the fever left her
MAT-018.alt: Jesus holds the hand of Peter’s restored mother-in-law as Peter watches gratefully beside her bed.

MAT-016.title: Jesus Calls Matthew
MAT-016.q: he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
MAT-016.alt: Jesus invites Matthew to leave his tax booth, where coins and a closed account roll rest on a low desk.
MAT-016.note: The collector’s booth, working table and coin denominations are reconstructed; the table is not a dining arrangement.

MAT-019.title: The Mustard Seed and the Tree
MAT-019.q: the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.
MAT-019.alt: Small birds shelter in a large flowering mustard plant above a Galilean garden.
MAT-019.note: A selected mustard-type visualization of the parable; the text does not uniquely establish its botanical species or a photographic seed scale.

MAT-020.title: The Pearl of Great Value
MAT-020.q: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
MAT-020.alt: A merchant admires a single pearl above dark cloth on his market table.
MAT-020.note: The prop was conservatively omitted; this is not a categorical dating claim for all ancient balances.

MAT-008.title: Jesus Walks on the Water
MAT-008.q: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
MAT-008.alt: Jesus approaches a wooden boat across rough lake water in dark predawn light; Peter remains inside at the selected moment before stepping out.
MAT-008.note: Selected moment Matthew 14:24-27, before Peter steps out of the boat.

MAT-021.title: Peter’s Confession
MAT-021.q: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
MAT-021.alt: Peter speaks to Jesus beside a stream near Caesarea Philippi.

MAT-009.title: The Transfiguration
MAT-009.q: his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
MAT-009.alt: Jesus shines in white linen between Moses and Elijah on a rocky mountain while three adult disciples watch.

MAT-010.title: The Entry into Jerusalem
MAT-010.q: Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord
MAT-010.alt: Jesus rides a donkey toward Jerusalem as a joyful crowd lays cloaks and palm branches along the road.
MAT-010.note: Matthew 21 includes the ass and colt. Riding the colt with the mother accompanying is the selected narrative visualization.

MAT-011.title: The Temple Courtyard
MAT-011.q: overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves
MAT-011.alt: Jesus stands firmly beside overturned money tables and scattered coins in the Temple court, with adults stepping back.
MAT-011.note: A selected aftermath of the cleansing. The Temple facade and complete court layout are interpretive, not measured reconstructions.

MAT-025.title: Ten Virgins Wait with Their Lamps
MAT-025.q: ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.
MAT-025.alt: Ten women wait at night in two groups of five, each with a lamp; five reserve oil flasks stand beside the left group.
MAT-025.note: Parable illustration, selected waiting stage before sleep. Small clay oil lamps are the chosen visual interpretation; five women have reserve vessels, whose oil is not directly visible. Costumes and courtyard are reconstructed.

MAT-026.title: The Ready Women Enter with the Bridegroom
MAT-026.q: they that were ready went in with him to the marriage
MAT-026.alt: Five women carrying lit lamps enter the open wedding gate as the bridegroom welcomes them.
MAT-026.note: Parable illustration of verse10, immediately before the door shuts. Only the five ready women are shown entering; the other five are away buying oil. The groom is an anonymous parable actor.

MAT-027.title: The Master Entrusts His Wealth
MAT-027.q: unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one
MAT-027.alt: A master seated on a pale stone bench hands a tied sack to one of three servants; other graded sacks lie nearby.
MAT-027.note: Parable illustration of the master entrusting goods before departure (Matthew 25:14-15). The stated talent sums remain textual; contained wealth and a few unmarked metal pieces do not visually certify exact weights or coin counts. The same anonymous actors continue in the later accounting scene.

MAT-028.title: The Servants Give Account
MAT-028.q: I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth
MAT-028.alt: A servant returns a soiled tied sack to a master seated on a stone bench as two other servants watch.
MAT-028.note: Parable illustration of the accounting in Matthew 25:19-27, before the later punishment. Contained money does not certify the stated talent sums. The same four anonymous actors and stone courtyard setting continue from the handover scene.

MAT-012.title: Prayer in Gethsemane
MAT-012.q: O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me
MAT-012.alt: Jesus kneels among old olive trees in Gethsemane at night while three adult disciples sleep at a distance.
MAT-012.note: Selected prayer span rather than the precise face-on-ground instant of Matthew 26:39. Downcast irises and sleeping disciples' fine faces are not assessable.

MAT-013.title: Torches in the Garden
MAT-013.alt: Jesus stands calmly among olive trees as torchbearers approach and Judas stands nearby, with no active violence.

MAT-022.title: The Women Meet the Risen Jesus
MAT-022.q: they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.
MAT-022.alt: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary kneel gratefully beside the risen Jesus on a dawn path.

MAT-014.title: The Great Commission
MAT-014.q: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations
MAT-014.alt: Jesus speaks to exactly eleven adult disciples on a hopeful Galilean mountainside beside the lake.

MRK-010.title: Jesus Restores the Man Who Kneels
MRK-010.q: put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.
MRK-010.alt: Jesus touches the man kneeling before him in a low flat-roofed Galilean village.
MRK-010.note: Jesus touches the man who kneels before him, shown at the moment of restoration (Mark 1:40–42). The modest Galilean setting is contextual reconstruction.

MRK-001.title: The Paralytic Is Restored
MRK-001.q: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all
MRK-001.alt: A restored adult man rises with his rolled bedmat beside Jesus in a crowded Capernaum room, roof opening above.

MRK-006.title: The Sower Goes Out
MRK-006.q: Behold, there went out a sower to sow
MRK-006.alt: A farmer scatters grain across a field beside a path, rocks and thorny ground.

MRK-002.title: Peace over the Storm
MRK-002.q: Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
MRK-002.alt: Jesus stands calmly with his disciples in a wooden boat as lake water settles and storm clouds retreat.
MRK-002.note: Mark 4:35 begins in the evening; exact crossing duration is not asserted. Fine irises and full disciple attendance are outside what this view certifies.

MRK-003.title: Jairus’s Daughter Restored
MRK-003.q: he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi
MRK-003.alt: Jesus holds the hand of Jairus daughter as she sits upright with her parents beside her. Peter, James and John watch from the doorway.
MRK-003.note: Doorway faces and downcast Jesus irises have visibility limits. The wider frame makes the named attendance explicit without claiming the old close crop proved their absence.

MRK-009.title: Jesus at the Carpenter’s Bench
MRK-009.q: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary
MRK-009.alt: In an interpretive workshop scene, Jesus works at a carpenter’s bench with period hand tools in a modest Nazareth setting.
MRK-009.note: Interpretive biography: Jesus at a carpenter’s bench, drawing on Mark 6:3. The verse names his occupation but does not narrate this specific workshop moment; the modest Nazareth setting and tools are reconstructed.

MRK-011.title: The Man Hears and Speaks
MRK-011.q: straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
MRK-011.alt: A restored man hears birds and speaks joyfully beside Jesus, with companions at a distance.
MRK-011.note: Shows the man’s joy after hearing is restored, apart from distant bystanders. His eye color and ancestry are not specified by the passage.

MRK-004.title: Jesus Welcomes the Children
MRK-004.q: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not
MRK-004.alt: Jesus sits warmly greeting modestly clothed children while parents stand nearby in a safe village courtyard.

MRK-007.title: The Rich Young Man’s Question
MRK-007.q: Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
MRK-007.alt: A richly dressed young man kneels before Jesus on a village road.
MRK-007.note: Shows the questioner before his sorrowful departure; background trees and buildings are contextual, not a precise location.

MRK-012.title: Bartimaeus Answers the Call
MRK-012.q: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.
MRK-012.alt: Bartimaeus rises beside the Jericho road and turns gratefully toward Jesus, his cloak left behind.
MRK-012.note: This selects Mark 10:52 after Bartimaeus receives sight.

MRK-008.title: The Withered Fig Tree
MRK-008.q: Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.
MRK-008.alt: Peter points toward a withered fig tree as Jesus speaks about faith and prayer.

MRK-005.title: The Widow’s Offering
MRK-005.q: she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.
MRK-005.alt: A poor widow drops two small coins into the temple treasury as Jesus watches.
MRK-005.note: Generic treasury receptacle is a contextual interpretation, not a measured Temple collection box. Fine iris detail is limited.

LUK-001.title: The Annunciation
LUK-001.q: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.
LUK-001.alt: Young adult Jewish Mary with olive-brown oval face, dark eyes, cream head covering and blue-gray mantle listens in wonder to Gabriel, a dignified white-robed messenger, in a modest stone Nazareth courtyard. Soft natural light, no halos.
LUK-001.note: Courtyard and village are contextual reconstructions; the shrub is not identified as a particular species.

LUK-002.title: Mary Visits Elizabeth
LUK-002.q: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
LUK-002.alt: Young Mary greets older Elizabeth, whose rounded clothed abdomen suggests pregnancy, outside a modest Judean home.
LUK-002.note: Young Mary greets elderly Elizabeth in the Judean hill country; Elizabeth’s pregnancy is visibly suggested by her rounded clothed abdomen (Luke 1:36,39–45). The greeting pose, dress and house are reconstructed.

LUK-003.title: The Nativity
LUK-003.q: wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger
LUK-003.alt: Same Mary and bearded adult Joseph in earth-brown robe and tan headscarf lovingly watch securely swaddled newborn Jesus lying safely in a straw-lined manger. Rough stone shelter and warm oil lamp; no Magi.
LUK-003.note: Manger material, shelter layout and distant lamplight are artistic reconstructions.

LUK-004.title: The Shepherds Visit
LUK-004.q: found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
LUK-004.alt: Modestly dressed adult shepherds visit the established Holy Family and securely swaddled infant manger in a humble stone shelter. Natural sheep behind, quiet joyful night, no Magi or royal gifts.
LUK-004.note: Shepherd count, sheep breed and shelter setting are interpretive.

LUK-017.title: The Angel and the Shepherds
LUK-017.q: Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy
LUK-017.alt: Shepherds and sheep watch a radiant white-robed angel on a Judean hillside beneath stars and a distant heavenly host.
LUK-017.note: The host is a visionary visualization; sheep breed, host count and distant lighting are unspecified.

LUK-005.title: Jesus Presented at the Temple
LUK-005.q: Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God
LUK-005.alt: Elderly Simeon securely cradles the swaddled infant with head supported and face uncovered while established Mary, Joseph and elderly Anna look on gratefully in the Jerusalem temple courtyard.
LUK-005.note: Bird species and measured Temple layout are not certified. Offering is contextual rather than a required simultaneous hand position during Simeon speech.

LUK-018.title: The Family Returns to Nazareth
LUK-018.q: they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
LUK-018.alt: Mary carries infant Jesus beside Joseph as the family returns to modest Nazareth houses after the purification.
LUK-018.note: This selects Luke 2:39’s transition after purification, with Jesus as an infant. Exact elapsed age and harmonization with Matthew are not established by the image.

LUK-006.title: Jesus Among the Teachers
LUK-006.q: sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
LUK-006.alt: Twelve-year-old Jesus, clean-faced and fully clothed with youthful proportions, sits safely among adult teachers discussing scrolls in the temple court. Mary and Joseph arrive relieved, naturally aged twelve years.
LUK-006.note: Scroll writing and complete Temple court layout are unassessable. Ancient rollers are not categorically prohibited.

LUK-019.title: Jesus Reads in Nazareth
LUK-019.q: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
LUK-019.alt: Jesus reads an opened scroll at a simple desk in a stone Nazareth synagogue while adults listen.
LUK-019.note: The assembly room and scroll completion are reconstructed. Ornate finials were simplified; this does not assert that all ancient wooden scroll rollers were impossible.

LUK-007.title: The Fishermen Are Called
LUK-007.q: Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
LUK-007.alt: Peter kneels at Jesus knees inside one of two fish-laden boats. James and John lift nets in the other boat, with water visible between the hulls.
LUK-007.note: Exact catch quantity, distant town and fine background facial details are not certified. James is a newly established artistic actor based on the original rear-left fisherman.

LUK-020.title: The Fishermen Leave Their Nets
LUK-020.q: they forsook all, and followed him.
LUK-020.alt: James, Peter and John walk after Jesus along the shore, leaving two boats and nets behind.
LUK-020.note: James and John reuse LUK-007 designs; exact portrait ages and full lakeside site are not certified. The earlier two-person crop did not establish absence from the event.

LUK-022.title: The Crowd Seeks Healing
LUK-022.q: the whole multitude sought to touch him
LUK-022.alt: Jesus holds a seated elder’s hand while families wait on level Galilean ground.
LUK-022.note: A close encounter represents part of the gathering on the plain; full crowd and precise site are outside the frame.

LUK-028.title: The Widow of Nain Receives Her Son
LUK-028.q: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
LUK-028.alt: Jesus presents the living young man to his relieved mother beside a stopped bier outside Nain.
LUK-028.note: Shows reunion after the young man sits up. The gate is contextual, rather than an excavated Nain reconstruction.

LUK-029.title: Forgiveness at Simon’s Table
LUK-029.q: Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
LUK-029.alt: At Simon’s meal Jesus turns compassionately toward an unnamed woman with an alabaster vessel near his feet.
LUK-029.note: Luke 7’s woman is unnamed here; she is not identified as either Mary.

LUK-024.title: Jesus Sends the Messengers
LUK-024.q: sent them two and two before his face into every city and place
LUK-024.alt: Jesus sends messengers out in pairs along a path toward nearby villages.
LUK-024.note: A few pairs represent the larger mission; buildings and route are contextual.

LUK-008.title: The Good Samaritan
LUK-008.q: bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast
LUK-008.alt: A Samaritan steadies a bandaged adult traveler safely seated on a donkey along a stony road, offering care.
LUK-008.note: An illustrative parable location, not a recovered road site or an ancestry claim.

LUK-011.title: Mary and Martha
LUK-011.q: which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word
LUK-011.alt: Jesus teaches in a modest Bethany home while Mary listens near his feet and Martha holds a bread tray.
LUK-011.note: Dates and olives are a conservative prop choice; the edit does not establish that apples were impossible in the ancient Mediterranean.

LUK-010.title: The Lost Sheep Is Found
LUK-010.q: he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
LUK-010.alt: An anonymous shepherd carries a sheep across both shoulders in rocky wilderness, with its head and hindquarters at opposite sides.
LUK-010.note: A visualization of the lost-sheep parable: an anonymous shepherd carries the found ewe across his shoulders, rejoicing (Luke 15:5). The sheep has a coherent body, four visible hooves and a separate broad tail. The regional fat-tailed type is comparative reconstruction; the ninety-nine remain off frame.

LUK-023.title: The Lost Coin Is Found
LUK-023.q: Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
LUK-023.alt: A woman holds up a found silver coin as her neighbors rejoice at the doorway.

LUK-009.title: The Prodigal Son Returns
LUK-009.q: his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
LUK-009.alt: An elderly father warmly embraces his adult younger son in dusty robes outside the family home.
LUK-009.note: The father welcomes his son before the feast; estate and flock are contextual parable details.

LUK-021.title: The Grateful Samaritan Returns
LUK-021.q: fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks
LUK-021.alt: A grateful Samaritan kneels before Jesus on a village path.
LUK-021.note: Shows the thankful return and conversation; others are outside this scene and the village is unidentified.

LUK-033.title: The Persistent Widow Petitions the Judge
LUK-033.q: she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.
LUK-033.alt: An older widow petitions with open hands as a seated judge listens with weary reluctance.
LUK-033.note: Parable illustration of one representative petition. The text supplies the widow’s persistence, not a count of visits or an exact court design; those appearances are reconstructed.

LUK-034.title: The Pharisee and the Publican Pray
LUK-034.q: smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.
LUK-034.alt: A publican lowers his head and holds a fist at his breast apart from an upright Pharisee in a columned court with a tall gilded sanctuary behind.
LUK-034.note: The Pharisee and publican pray apart in a visualization of Luke 18:9-14: the publican lowers his eyes and strikes his breast. The people and court setting are interpretive. The partly obscured Herodian sanctuary uses the project’s selected later-Middot model as a visual guide; its painted perspective does not establish exact dimensions or a complete plan.

LUK-012.title: Zacchaeus in the Sycamore
LUK-012.q: climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him
LUK-012.alt: Zacchaeus sits securely on a broad low sycamore branch, looking toward Jesus and a crowd below in Jericho.
LUK-012.note: The selected tree model follows sycomore-fig morphology. Synthetic leaves do not certify a particular specimen, and Zacchaeus’s stature cannot be measured while seated.

LUK-025.title: Jesus Looks Over Jerusalem
LUK-025.q: he beheld the city, and wept over it
LUK-025.alt: Jesus weeps as he looks over Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives.
LUK-025.note: Intentionally simplified hazy skyline, not a complete measured AD 30 Jerusalem reconstruction. Oblique wet iris hue unassessable.

LUK-013.title: The Last Supper
LUK-013.q: he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it
LUK-013.alt: Jesus gives thanks over bread and wine at a low table with exactly twelve apostles, thirteen men in the upper room.

LUK-014.title: Peter in the Courtyard
LUK-014.q: while he yet spake, the cock crew.
LUK-014.alt: Peter sits troubled beside a charcoal fire in a stone courtyard, with a rooster on the wall and dawn approaching.
LUK-014.note: Shows Peter’s troubled pause by the fire; courtyard fixtures and skyline are contextual, rather than a measured residence.

LUK-030.title: Jesus Before the Council
LUK-030.q: Art thou then the Son of God? And he said unto them, Ye say that I am.
LUK-030.alt: Jesus stands with dignity before seated council elders in a Jerusalem stone chamber at dawn.

LUK-031.title: Simon Carries the Cross
LUK-031.q: on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.
LUK-031.alt: Jesus walks ahead as Simon of Cyrene carries a rough crossbeam through a Jerusalem street.
LUK-031.note: A close view of Simon carrying the crossbeam after Jesus. Escorts are outside the frame and skyline is contextual.

LUK-015.title: The Crucifixion
LUK-015.q: there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.
LUK-015.alt: Three distant crosses stand on a rocky hill beneath a darkened sky, with fully clothed adult witnesses nearby.

LUK-026.title: The Women at the Empty Tomb
LUK-026.q: Why seek ye the living among the dead?
LUK-026.alt: Mary Magdalene and two women meet two white-robed messengers at the empty tomb at dawn.
LUK-026.note: Bowed full faces and irises unassessable. Three visible women are a selected group, not a full attendance count. Round stone and rich tomb form are interpretive, not an identified historical tomb.

LUK-016.title: The Road to Emmaus
LUK-016.q: Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.
LUK-016.alt: Jesus walks beside exactly two adult disciples through the Judean hills in late-afternoon conversation.
LUK-016.note: Evening road conversation in Luke 24:13–29; no exact archaeological Emmaus location is asserted.

LUK-032.title: Recognized in the Breaking of Bread
LUK-032.q: their eyes were opened, and they knew him
LUK-032.alt: Jesus breaks bread at Emmaus as the same two travelers from the road recognize him.
LUK-032.note: Luke 24:30–32 names bread without specifying its thickness; this view does not certify visible wounds.

LUK-027.title: Peace Among the Disciples
